summary: Server singleton backed by a savegame model (ls::model::game::inventory::v0::LootableReactionQueueSingletonComponent): two hash sets. Seen once in an idle level, empty.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Windows save loader bg3.exe+0x25C2290 (model game.inventory.v0.LootableReactionQueueSingletonComponent, 32 bytes = two arrays; the only other model saved with it is ls::model::core::v0::EntityId) converts the model with bg3.exe+0x2779F90 into two 48-byte hash sets and moves the first into component +0..+0x30. bg3.exe+0x2779F90 builds the set from 8-byte elements (count = byte size >> 3, bucket = key % bucket count on the full 8 bytes, keys stored at +0x20) - entity handles. Destructor FUN_1406c6a10 frees both with the HashSet destructor FUN_140582AD0. Live: empty.

fields.name: field_30
fields.evidence: Second set, built by bg3.exe+0x2779F90 from the second model array (same 8-byte EntityId elements) and moved to +0x30 by the loader bg3.exe+0x25C2290.

open_questions: Roles of the two sets: no system reads or writes the component on macOS or in bg3.exe outside the creator, the destructor and the save loader/saver (it may be dead data kept for old saves).
second_pass: The Windows save loader bg3.exe+0x25C2290 and its converter bg3.exe+0x2779F90 settle both members as HashSet<EntityHandle> at +0 and +0x30 (model of two EntityId arrays); the names stay unknown because no system uses the component.
live_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
